Paragraph:
Translation: The demigods, being pleased by sacrifices, will also please you; thus nourishing one another, there will reign general prosperity for all.

Purport (Excerpt): ...Their pleasures and displeasures are dependant on the performance of yajnas by the human being... When these yajnas are perfectly performed, naturally the demigods in charge of the different departments of supply are pleased, and there is no scarcity... by performance of yajna, one's eatables become sanctified, and by eating sanctified foodstuffs, one's very existence becomes purified...
Situation/Problem_Faced: Maintaining balance and abundance between humanity and environmental/cosmic systems.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna describes mutual symbiosis (parasparam bhavayantah): humans honor cosmic caretakers through sacrifice, and in turn, natural forces nourish humanity, leading to universal prosperity.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna understands that human prosperity depends on reciprocal cooperation with nature and higher powers rather than unilateral exploitation.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Mutual Symbiosis: Fostering mutually beneficial relationships with one's surroundings
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Interconnectedness: Recognizing that personal well-being is tied to environmental and social harmony
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Abundance Mindset: Cultivating trust in shared exchange rather than hoarding resources out of fear

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Parasparam bhavayantah (Mutual nourishment and reciprocal cooperation)
Sreyah param avapsyatha (Attaining the supreme good through reciprocal sacrifice)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Sacrifice establishes a reciprocal bond between humanity and the demigods (cosmic administrators). By offering sacrifice, humans please the forces of nature, which respond with natural abundance, creating a harmonious cycle of prosperity and spiritual elevation.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Psychological health flourishes when we view our environment through a lens of give-and-take rather than extraction. Reciprocity—contributing positively to your community, environment, and relationships—replaces isolation with a sense of security and mutual support.
